title: EyeGraph: A Multi-granularity Medical Vision-Language Foundation Model with Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Ophthalmic Interpretation.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on medical imaging
zh_title: EyeGraph：眼科多模态视觉语言基础模型
summary: IEEE TMI 论文提出结合知识图谱推理的眼科视觉语言模型 EyeGraph，并发布多粒度眼科 VQA 数据集 IT-Retinal。
abstract: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] The exponential growth of large vision-language models (VLMs) has created significant opportunities for advancing multimodal artificial intelligence in specialized domains such as ophthalmology. However, progress in ophthalmic VLMs remains limited, primarily due to the lack of large-scale, high-quality image-text pairs. Moreover, existing VLMs frequently generate hallucinations, leading to uncertainty and unreliability that are unacceptable in clinical practice. To address the data scarcity issue, we introduce IT-Retinal, a dedicated ophthalmic Vision Question Answering (VQA) dataset that providesmultigranularity tasks and high-quality long-form textual content in image-text pairs. To mitigate hallucinations, we propose EyeGraph, a framework for ophthalmic VLMs that consists of two training stages, targeted pre-training and fine-tuning, and one inference stage that integrates Graph of Thought (GoT) and Think on Graph (ToG) reasoning, referred to as G2T. This design enables EyeGraph to incorporate structured external knowledge, constrain the output space, and produce more clinically consistent results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EyeGraph achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven clinically relevant benchmarks, spanning disease diagnosis, structural detection and localization, and report generation. Notably, the proposed G2T reasoning module consistently improves the factual consistency and reliability of ophthalmic report generation. All source code, along with an interactive demo, is publicly available at: https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph.

zh_abstract: [IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging] 大型视觉-语言模型（vision-language models, VLMs）的指数级增长为在眼科等专业领域推进多模态人工智能创造了重要机遇。然而，眼科VLMs的进展仍然有限，主要原因是缺乏大规模、高质量的图像-文本对。此外，现有VLMs经常产生幻觉，导致临床实践中不可接受的不确定性和不可靠性。为解决数据稀缺问题，我们引入IT-Retinal，这是一个专门的眼科视觉问答（Vision Question Answering, VQA）数据集，在图像-文本对中提供多粒度任务和高质量长文本内容。为减轻幻觉，我们提出EyeGraph，这是一个用于眼科VLMs的框架，包含两个训练阶段——有针对性的预训练和微调——以及一个推理阶段，该推理阶段整合了思维图（Graph of Thought, GoT）和图上思考（Think on Graph, ToG）推理，称为G2T。这一设计使EyeGraph能够纳入结构化外部知识、约束输出空间，并产生更具临床一致性的结果。大量实验表明，EyeGraph在七个临床相关基准上达到最先进性能，涵盖疾病诊断、结构检测与定位以及报告生成。值得注意的是，所提出的G2T推理模块持续提高了眼科报告生成的事实一致性和可靠性。所有源代码以及交互式演示均公开可用，地址为：https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph。

abstract: [Computational and structural biotechnology journal] Bladder cancer ranks as the 10th most common malignancy worldwide. Advances in technology are continuously reshaping its diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognosis assessment. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated marked potential in transforming bladder cancer care. By integrating and analyzing multi-source data, AI enhances the precision and efficiency of disease management. This review comprehensively examines the current applications of AI across various domains, including radiographic imaging analysis, pathological diagnosis, cystoscopic image processing, molecular subtyping, drug development, organoid research, prognostic modeling, and medical device innovation. It highlights the advantages of AI over conventional methods, outlines model development strategies, and summarizes commonly employed algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges in translating AI tools into real-world clinical practice. This narrative review aims to inform the future development of AI-driven digital health systems, ultimately contributing to the realization of precision medicine and personalized management for bladder cancer patients.
zh_abstract: [《计算与结构生物技术杂志》] 膀胱癌是全球第10大常见恶性肿瘤。技术进步正在持续重塑其诊断、治疗选择和预后评估。近年来，人工智能（AI）在改变膀胱癌诊疗方面展现出显著潜力。通过整合和分析多源数据，AI提高了疾病管理的精准性和效率。本综述全面审视了AI在多个领域的当前应用，包括放射影像分析、病理诊断、膀胱镜图像处理、分子分型、药物研发、类器官研究、预后建模和医疗器械创新。文章强调了AI相对于传统方法的优势，概述了模型开发策略，并总结了常用算法。此外，我们讨论了将AI工具转化为真实世界临床实践中的关键挑战。这篇叙述性综述旨在为AI驱动的数字健康系统的未来发展提供信息，最终有助于实现膀胱癌患者的精准医学和个性化管理。

abstract: Clinical care, health-system operations and biomedical discovery depend on extracting reliable answers from patient records, yet applying diverse clinical questions across entire populations remains computationally expensive. Here we present Clinical System One (CS1), a 4-billion-parameter decision model for fast, typed judgments from clinical records, along with two agentic harnesses in which CS1 works together with a generalist language model. CS1-4B is trained on 12.4 million questions and answers from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system, combining structured-data keys, observed outcomes and language-model supervision across clinical notes, diagnostic reports and patient timelines. It answers multiple typed questions in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining, and each answer carries a probability that can route uncertain cases to human review. On 963,408 held-out patients, CS1-4B outperformed open decision models up to 27 billion parameters on 13 of 14 tasks scored independently of its training teacher. Across 21 external data sets, its aggregate performance approached that of the strongest tested 27-billion-parameter model, with 6.4-fold faster inference in a matched workload. Integrating CS1-4B with a language model agent produced cited answers over complete multi-year patient histories and screened a patient population against the eligibility criteria of 17 registered clinical trials, placing four times as many judged-eligible patients among its top 20 candidates as keyword search while using 690-fold fewer language-model tokens than a language model reading every record. These findings support a division of labour in clinical AI, with small decision models performing repeated record reading and generative models formulating questions and synthesizing evidence.
zh_abstract: 临床诊疗、卫生系统运营和生物医学发现依赖于从患者记录中提取可靠的答案，然而在整个人群中应用多样化的临床问题仍然计算成本高昂。在此，我们提出Clinical System One（CS1），一个40亿参数的决策模型，用于从临床记录中进行快速、类型化判断，以及两个智能体框架，在其中CS1与通用语言模型协同工作。CS1-4B在来自一个多医院卫生系统360万名患者的1240万个问题与答案上进行训练，结合了结构化数据键、观察结局以及在临床笔记、诊断报告和患者时间线上的语言模型监督。它无需任务特定的再训练，便可在单次前向传播中回答多个类型化问题，并且每个答案都带有概率，可将不确定病例转交人工复核。在963,408名留出患者上，CS1-4B在14项任务中的13项上优于参数量最高达270亿的开放式决策模型，这些任务独立于其训练教师进行评分。在21个外部数据集上，其总体性能接近测试过的最强270亿参数模型，并在匹配工作负载下推理速度快6.4倍。将CS1-4B与语言模型智能体整合后，可基于完整的多年患者病史生成带引用的答案，并依据17项注册临床试验的入组标准筛选患者人群，在其前20名候选者中判定为符合条件的患者数量是关键词搜索的4倍，同时使用的语言模型token比阅读每份记录的语言模型少690倍。这些发现支持临床AI中的分工，即小型决策模型执行重复的记录阅读，生成式模型提出问题并综合证据。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Catharina Ziekenhuis Eindhoven; conditions: Ovarian Cancer, Ovarian Tumor, Borderline Ovarian Tumor; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 1300; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] The goal of this observational study is to learn if a computer program can tell what type of ovarian tumour a person has from a CT scan taken before surgery. The program uses artificial intelligence (AI). It sorts tumours into three groups: * benign: not cancer * borderline: abnormal cells that usually behave less aggressively than cancer * malignant: cancer Before surgery, doctors try to judge which group a tumour belongs to. This guides where and how the operation is done. This judgement is often hard, especially for borderline tumours. An AI program that does it well could help doctors plan surgery. The main questions it aims to answer are: * How well does the AI program sort ovarian tumours into benign, borderline and malignant on CT scans? * Does the AI program work as well on scans from hospitals it did not learn from? Researchers will compare the AI program's results with the final diagnosis from the tumour tissue removed during surgery. They will also compare the program with methods doctors use today, such as ultrasound-based risk scores and the radiologist's report. In a smaller group, researchers will test the program on MRI scans. This study only uses information that already exists. It includes adults who had surgery for a mass in or near the ovary at hospitals in the Netherlands and Belgium. Researchers will use: * CT or MRI scans made before surgery as part of regular care * information from medical records * the tissue diagnosis after surgery Participants will not be contacted. They will not have any extra scans, tests or visits. Each hospital codes the data before sharing them, so researchers cannot see participants' names. The study does not change anyone's care.
zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办方：Catharina Ziekenhuis Eindhoven；疾病：卵巢癌、卵巢肿瘤、交界性卵巢肿瘤；类型：观察性；入组人数：1300；状态：尚未招募] 这项观察性研究的目标是了解计算机程序能否根据术前CT扫描判断一个人患有何种类型的卵巢肿瘤。该程序使用人工智能（AI）。它将肿瘤分为三组：* 良性：不是癌症 * 交界性：异常细胞，通常比癌症侵袭性低 * 恶性：癌症 术前，医生会尝试判断肿瘤属于哪一组。这指导手术在哪里以及如何进行。这种判断通常很困难，尤其是对交界性肿瘤。一个能很好完成此任务的AI程序可以帮助医生规划手术。它旨在回答的主要问题是：* AI程序在CT扫描上将卵巢肿瘤分为良性、交界性和恶性的效果如何？* AI程序在它未学习过的医院扫描图像上是否也同样有效？研究人员将把AI程序的结果与手术中切除的肿瘤组织的最终诊断进行比较。他们还将把该程序与医生目前使用的方法进行比较，例如基于超声的风险评分和放射科医生的报告。在较小的一组人群中，研究人员将在MRI扫描上测试该程序。这项研究仅使用已经存在的信息。它包括在荷兰和比利时的医院因卵巢内或卵巢附近肿块接受手术的成年人。研究人员将使用：* 作为常规护理一部分的术前CT或MRI扫描 * 病历中的信息 * 手术后的组织诊断 参与者不会被联系。他们不会接受任何额外的扫描、检查或访视。每家医院在共享数据前会对数据进行编码，因此研究人员无法看到参与者的姓名。该研究不会改变任何人的护理。
